author: 2Yung4This
title: One of the most overhyped piece of media
content: *Stranger Things* started off in a solid place I loved this show when it came out, it felt fresh at the time-simple, focused, and driven by mystery rather than spectacle. Seasons 1 and 2 are easily the strongest because the story was contained, the cast was small, and the tone felt natural. The kids felt like actual kids, the danger felt real, and the show knew when to hold back instead of constantly trying to escalate.After that, the series clearly overstays its welcome. The concept gets stretched thinner with every season, yet Netflix takes years between releases for seasons that are only 8-9 episodes long. The wait is never justified by what we actually get. Over time, the show became one of the most overhyped pieces of media in recent years while mostly hovering around average in terms of writing and structure.The biggest issue is the complete lack of stakes. The writers are visibly afraid to kill off any main characters, which removes all tension. The core cast survives absurd, impossible situations again and again, so there is never a real sense of danger. Instead, the show relies on killing disposable new characters or faceless soldiers to fake consequences. When viewers know the main characters are untouchable, nothing feels earned.This problem is perfectly summed up by Max's storyline. Her arc was emotionally complete and thematically appropriate for a tragic ending, yet the show refuses to commit. Keeping her alive adds no meaningful narrative value and only reinforces the feeling that the writers will not follow through on consequences. It feels less like a creative decision and more like a refusal to let go of popular characters. As a result, the story loses weight, and emotional moments feel hollow.The growing cast also works against the show. There are now too many characters, many of whom have very little to do but are kept around anyway. Instead of tightening the story, the show keeps expanding sideways. Characters who once felt essential now feel like background filler, hanging around because the show does not know how to move on from them.The adults are another weak point. Their behavior makes little sense as the series progresses. Allowing children to repeatedly handle world-ending threats is already hard to believe, but the decision for families to continue living in Hawkins-after it becomes an obvious supernatural disaster zone-is absurd. The idea that the government or military would allow people to remain there completely breaks immersion. These choices make the plot feel sloppy and convenient rather than thought-out.The characters themselves also lose their charm over time. They worked in the first two seasons because they were kids dealing with something far bigger than themselves. As they grow older, the writing does not evolve with them. Many of them feel out of place, underwritten, or stuck repeating the same beats, relying more on nostalgia than strong character development.Zooming out, this fits a larger Netflix pattern. The platform frequently cancels creative or well-written shows while continuing to push popular but mediocre ones. The focus seems to be on engagement numbers and brand recognition rather than long-term quality. With Netflix expanding further into major studio properties, the trend does not inspire confidence for the future of mainstream entertainment.Overall, *Stranger Things* is not a terrible show, but it is far from the masterpiece it is often presented as. It peaked early, dragged on far too long, and lost its sense of danger along the way. What started as a tight, mysterious story became bloated, safe, and predictable-and that is ultimately its biggest failure.

author: rayhansulaiman
title: Great show sadly let down by Noah Schnapps bad acting
content: Stranger Things has earned its reputation as one of Netflix's flagship series, blending nostalgia, mystery, and heartfelt character arcs into a consistently engaging story. The world-building remains top-tier, the visual effects continue to escalate in impressive ways, and much of the ensemble cast delivers compelling, emotionally grounded work.However, for me, the momentum of the show is noticeably interrupted by Noah Schnapp's performance as Will Byers. While the character is central to the emotional core of several seasons, his portrayal often feels stiff and underdeveloped compared to the high-caliber performances around him. In scenes requiring intense emotional expression, Schnapp's delivery can come across as forced or flat, making it harder to fully connect with Will's experiences and the weight the story places on him.This isn't to say Schnapp lacks talent or potential-he has moments where his acting lands, and it's clear he's committed to the role. But in a series where subtle, nuanced performances from the rest of the cast elevate the story, the inconsistency in Will's portrayal can be distracting.Stranger Things remains an entertaining and imaginative show, but for viewers who value character-driven storytelling above all, the unevenness in this particular performance may lessen its overall emotional impact.

author: ricarwuf
title: The Upside Down of Our Hearts
content: Stranger Things is a great TV show that matures alongside its protagonists. What truly makes the show shine are the characters. They're likable, relatable, and well-developed. I rarely connect with so many characters in a show, but here, I found myself genuinely caring for nearly all of them.One of its biggest achievements is how the show evolves as its young cast grows older, it reflects their development in tone, stakes, and emotional depth. Also, you can clearly see how the series became a top priority for Netflix, especially in the last two seasons, where the production value, special effects, and visuals show a massive investment.The acting is strong in general, which is impressive considering much of the main cast began as children. Millie Bobby Brown and Gaten Matarazzo stand out, and Jamie Campbell Bower brings a particularly great performance.Another of the show's strongest qualities, and something still quite rare in sci-fi, is how many of the main characters are women. From Eleven's power and vulnerability, to Max's emotional arc, to Joyce's fierce determination, the series is packed with complex, resilient, and central female figures. These characters drive the narrative just as much (if not more) than their male counterparts.The story itself is engaging and fueled by 1980s nostalgia, especially rewarding for those who grew up in that era. However, the plot is also one of the show's weaker aspects. There are inconsistencies and noticeable plot holes. It sometimes feels like the writers were building the narrative as they went, rather than following a clear arc planned across five seasons from the beginning. Still, this doesn't ruin the experience. Stranger Things is not meant to be airtight science fiction, instead it's an emotional and fun adventure, mainly targeted at teenagers and young adults.From the '80s references to the soundtrack, from the effects to the sense of geeky wonder, Stranger Things is ultimately a great watch. It may not be flawless, but it delivers entertainment, emotion, and style in a way few shows have since Game of Thrones. I liked the ending and the final season and all the show in general. I highly recommend it.Don't go in expecting a heavy or overly serious show, this is more about heart and thrills. And in that, it excels.

author: tobydale
title: Wonderful '80s homage
content: Season 1. My rating 9/10. Stranger Things is every bit as good as the hype. Wish I'd watched it sooner. It's engaging, fun, kinda scary but above all it's an absolutely spot on '80s homage. The storylines and the way this whole thing looks and works are so reminiscent of the early 1980s. There is a verging-on-cheesy naivety about it, but that's part of the charm!There's also something very David Lynch and voyeuristic about the way the lid is lifted on small-town America and all its horrors... I love it and will be continuing to binge!Not sure why I am getting thumbs down for the 9/10 rating I'm giving Stanger Things season 1!?Season 2. My rating 9/10. This moves on brilliantly from S1. There is character and relationship development which works well. We become attached and invested. This is about the kids, the adults are secondary to them and their worlds.Although it looks like it, Stranger Things is not "horror". The cleverness is in the fact that it can be any fear or anxiety we want it to be: fear of the unknown, anxiety about the opposite sex, anxiety about growing up. Each of the characters exhibits these, and manifests their reactions as they search for meaning and place in the world.Great stuff! The binge continues!Season 3. My rating 8/10. Although there is good action in this series - very good action, for me it doesn't stack up as high as the first two seasons.There is a little too much naivity now! It seems as if the characters haven't learned that Hawkins is a really dangerous place!The characters are also marking time - they are just carrying on doing what they do. Don't be mistaken - this is still a lot of fun, but after 15 hours I'd expect more.The other thing is - it's all a little bit Scooby-Doo. There are kids chasing around being kids and doing dumb things which they ought to have learned by now are not sensible things to do. Also, the cavalry always arrives in the nick of time to save the day. I wanted more.The binge continues....Season 4. My rating 10/10. Now I can really see why Stranger Things gets all the qudos! The season finale is FANTASTIC!!! It sits on top of all the previous episodes in all the series. Just this single episode is enough to score 10/10 from me!There are many stories; split-stream storytelling, which is done really well. There is still this childish naivety, which is obviously an intended feature. There is still Scooby-Doo type stuff, which works! But this series is oh so dark!The friendships and relationships really make this. The characters and their story arcs are really good.Wonderful 1980s music!Series 4 is really brilliant, and builds to this AWESOME final episode! I bit my fingernails down and had to go to the toilet four times!!!Bring on Season 5!!!!!!Season 5. My rating OMG! THIS IS GOLLY WICKED!!! 11/10Oh dear oh dear! If you get invested in Stranger Things (and I hope you do...), then Season 5 will completely blow you away. This is peerless. It's as good as anything that's ever been on TV.It ALL comes together BIG TIME!Alright there are lots of characters, alright the whole thing is a bit sprawling - but so what?You will be gripped. You will be entertained. You will laugh. You will cry. All the stories come together and are resolved. The friendships find their culminating expressions. This is deep. But it's fully in keeping with the whole of the Stranger Things franchise.The final 30 minutes are beautiful. The closing titles and music made me cry.For me the superlatives go as far as to say that Stranger Things creates it's own visual, audial and emotional language. It's unique and just brilliant. I feel sorry now that it's over.

author: IcyTones
title: Stranger Things Have Happened
content:
It's Strange how the continuity & flow of 'Stranger Things' is a little 'upside down'.What I liked about Seasons 1 and 2, was the seriousness with which it delivered & entertained.1. The major players were not the usual handful of boring suspects collaborating together: - ie: astronauts, Dr's, FBI agents, forensic detectives, geniuses, PI's - (ie: Private Investigators), scientists, secret agents or spies etc. They didn't have high IQs or come from super rich backgrounds, but they weren't 'plebs' either - (ie: of the lower social classes). They weren't religious, part of 'the-in crowd' or 'the it group'. These were your average middle-class kids. With the exception of Holly & Erica, these were pre-teens & teens. Their adventures reminded me of 'The Railway Children'. Set in the 1980s, Stranger Things held my attention as I 'took a trip down memory lane'.2. The acting from all of the cast was so superb & superior to anything else I'd seen in the past, especially from Dustin, Eleven, Erica & Lucas. There were no 'stiffs'. Hopper's lakeside lodge, 'Coffee & Contemplation' approach to life is worlds away from my own, that the show captivated my imagination. I could daydream about future possibilities of such a lifestyle.3. The very mention of 'Nam' - (short for Vietnam) - by Lucas, and 'Project MK Ultra' by Eleven's aunt, is/was a reminder and an educational testimony to another one of America's blunders and 'horrible history'. It therefore validated the series as 'pukka'.4. The episodes weren't used as a sales pitch or platform to showcase US allies or advances, strategies or strides the US have made in science & technology.
However, by 'not' displaying the future of America, via its array of military help & weaponry that kills 'the monster spy', this is probably what accounts for 95% of the lack of funding & interest from serious investors. Hence why Season 3 was a little different, but ultimately, what we've ended up with is sporadic seasons & disjointed episodes.My Star Ratings:
Season One: 10/10; Season Two: 10/10; Season Three: 2/10 - for effort; Season Four: 0/10 ???

author: BijoyB-14
title: From Kid to Grown-Up: My Emotional Journey with Stranger Things
content: What a journey this show has been.I still remember starting Stranger Things as a kid-coming home from school, turning on the screen without any expectations, just curiosity. Back then, I was just a boy watching a group of kids ride bikes, fight monsters, and stick together no matter what. I had no idea that years later, life would change so much. That boy grew up. He started earning for his family. Responsibilities replaced free afternoons. Time became heavier.But when I sat down to watch the final season, something magical happened.For those hours, I wasn't the tired man anymore. I was that kid again.That's the power of Stranger Things. It doesn't just tell a story-it carries you back to who you once were. The Duffer Brothers didn't just create a sci-fi show; they created a feeling, a memory, a piece of growing up that stayed with us. Every season felt like a chapter of our own lives, not just the characters'.Seeing these characters one last time hit hard. Winona Ryder's fierce, never-give-up Joyce. David Harbour's broken but brave Hopper. Millie Bobby Brown growing up right in front of our eyes as Eleven. Finn Wolfhard, Gaten Matarazzo, Caleb McLaughlin, and Noah Schnapp-watching Mike, Dustin, Lucas, and Will evolve from kids into young men felt personal. Sadie Sink's Max, Natalia Dyer's Nancy, Charlie Heaton's Jonathan, Joe Keery's Steve, Maya Hawke's Robin, Priah Ferguson's Erica, Brett Gelman's Murray, and Jamie Campbell Bower's unforgettable presence-all of them gave their hearts to this story.People will always have opinions. Some will say this, some will say that. But for people like me, *Stranger Things* was never just about the monsters, the Upside Down, or the theories. It was about friendship, growing up, loss, courage, and holding on to hope even when things get dark.For us, this wasn't just a show ending.It was an emotional journey reaching its final page.And honestly-it felt right. It felt true. It felt like a perfect goodbye.Thank you, Duffer Brothers.Thank you to the entire cast.Thank you for giving that kid from years ago a reason to smile again.This show will never just be a series to me.It will always be a memory.

author: AthenaG-49
title: I enjoyed every bit of it
content: I genuinely enjoyed the final season of Stranger Things, and I find most of the negative criticism surrounding it disconnected from reality.The story delivered what it had been building toward for years. The core questions of the series were answered, character arcs reached their conclusions, and the emotional payoff was earned. Yet, a portion of the audience seems to expect every microscopic detail to be explicitly explained... as if a story loses its value unless it functions like a checklist of answers. Why Vecna chose Will. Why the final battle was only ten minutes. Why every symbolic choice wasn't spelled out. Honestly, this kind of nitpicking misses the point.We used to watch films and series without demanding that every single detail be verbally justified. Not because storytelling was better back then, but because we weren't constantly exposed to endless online theories, overanalysis, and inflated expectations shaped by social media. Today, people don't judge the story that was told, they judge the story that didn't match the theories they consumed.Many viewers weren't disappointed by the season itself, but by the fact that the show didn't validate the exaggerated and often meaningless theories circulating online. And that's not a flaw of the writing. The essence of Stranger Things was always about character, emotion, and atmosphere, not about answering every "why" to satisfy internet discourse. All the important questions that mattered to the story were answered.If there is one valid criticism, it's not narrative-related at all: the wait. The three-year gap before the final season undeniably created distance, forgetfulness, and unrealistic expectations among fans. That long delay is what caused perceived "gaps," not poor storytelling.In the end, Stranger Things concluded its journey with heart, consistency, and respect for its characters. It didn't need to overexplain itself and it certainly didn't need to cater to every online theory to succeed.

author: MrA-219
title: Love this
content: Review: Stranger Things (300 words)Stranger Things is one of those rare shows that feels both nostalgic and fresh at the same time. Set in the 1980s, it blends supernatural mystery, science fiction, horror, humor, and heartfelt emotion into a gripping storyline. The show begins with the disappearance of a young boy named Will Byers, and from that moment, the series pulls viewers into the eerie and strange events happening in the small town of Hawkins, Indiana.The biggest strength of the show lies in its characters. The group of kids-Mike, Dustin, Lucas, and later Eleven-carry the emotional weight of the story. Their friendship feels real and natural, and the way they stick together despite fear and danger gives the show heart. Eleven, in particular, is one of the most compelling characters. Her mysterious past and supernatural powers instantly make her unforgettable.The adults and older teens are just as important. Joyce Byers, played by Winona Ryder, delivers a brilliant performance as a desperate mother determined to find her son. The evolving storylines of characters like Hopper, Steve, Nancy, and Max add depth and keep the series interesting across multiple seasons.Visually, Stranger Things captures the 80s perfectly-from the music and pop culture references to the costumes and cinematography. The show's creepy atmosphere, the tension of the Upside Down, and the terrifying design of creatures like the Demogorgon and Mind Flayer make it genuinely thrilling.What sets Stranger Things apart is its balance. It's scary, but not overwhelming; emotional, but not overly dramatic; nostalgic, yet original. Even with its supernatural elements, the show remains grounded in themes of friendship, courage, and growing up.Overall, Stranger Things is an addictive and well-crafted series that leaves a lasting impact, making it one of Netflix's most iconic shows.

title: Season 3 review
content:
Everything has led up to this big trilogy and even though it ends the only way it could, it could have simply omitted the end credits sequence. You have to film scenes a certain way in order to have the visual FX team do their best but it didn't fit the original style of the show. Now... of course the show steps up the action, big time... and it stepped up the consequences. There NEEDED to be BIG consequences and there was. There was a sense of dread in S3 missing from S2, which by far was the weakest even though it had it's pivotal scenes with Eleven. I felt some of the pacing/editing could have been altered before the BIG climax but that's just a personal choice. I loved the Never Ending story reference which does have meaning to the show. They might be telling us the story will never end because someone else is going to always try to get to the upside down, many of which didn't figure out with their hate of that moment. What happens in the actual Climax is brutal and unforgiving to the trilogy and I'm so glad some sequence didn't comeback to show us something REALLY stupid, which it didn't. The consequences of the town were unreal and really disturbing. Loved it.

How some people could think this has turned into some comedy/drama confuses the hell out of me to be honest. It felt the most brutal on honest episode.

author: BilalA-568
title: Fantastic
content: This is not just a show; it's a thunderous declaration that modern episodic storytelling can achieve cinematic heights. Stranger Things is a phenomenal achievement in every sense, delivering a powerful, emotionally charged, and visually stunning epic that deserves every bit of praise it receives. I give it a perfect 10/10.The Duffer Brothers' direction is masterful. They take nostalgic 80s aesthetics and re-imagine them with a gritty, dark, and grand scale befitting a modern blockbuster. The cinematography is breathtaking, creating a world that is brutal, beautiful (especially the Upside Down), and utterly immersive. The action sequences and VFX are meticulously executed-raw, impactful, and easily among the best ever produced on television. This is a show made with passion, patience, and uncompromising vision.The performances are truly the heart of this saga. Millie Bobby Brown as Eleven is hypnotic; her transformation from a silent, brooding captive to an explosive hero is flawless. But it is the chemistry among the core friend group (Finn Wolfhard, Gaten Matarazzo, Caleb McLaughlin, Noah Schnapp) that elevates the show to classic status. Their magnetic, terrifying friendship is the core dramatic force that anchors the supernatural horror.From the stirring synth-wave background score to the incredible production design that perfectly captures the early 80s, no expense was spared in making this look and feel authentic and monumental. It manages to balance visceral horror with genuine emotional depth, making you root for its tragic heroes until the very end.Stranger Things is a game-changer, setting a new benchmark for genre television. If you haven't watched it, you are missing out on a towering cinematic experience. Go watch it on the biggest screen possible.

author: kumadan
title: Season 3 Review (Spoiler Free)
content:
Disclaimer: As stated in the title this is a spoiler free review of Stranger Things Season 3 but I will be talking about plot points and minor spoilers from Season 1 & 2.So Stranger Things 3 picks up where we left off after season 2, everyone is happy and everyone is together, there is love in the air, it is the summer of love. Right off the bat I can say I preferred this season over season 2. This season felt more contained, it felt like it had a purpose and knew what it was doing and where is was going. Season 2 for me felt more of a mess, especially with "The Lost Sister" filler episode. The reviews of that episode tanked so hard that the writers completely gave up on that subplot, and I'm glad they did. That is one of the many reasons season 3 feels so much more crisp, because Matt and Ross Duffer decided to be more focused on the main story.As always the cast this season is great, the kids are now older and feel more like seasoned actors and much more mature in their performances. The kids stand out and shine more in this season especially with the addition of a couple of new characters. The adult characters are great as well, but a lot of them (apart from the main ones) felt wasted and underdeveloped. For example, in true 1980's form, we have evil Russians, which sounds hilarious but falls flat. The reason season 1 shined more than this or season 2 is because it had a well defined shadowy government department with a leader who was well developed. Remember "papa" from season 1? aka Dr. Martin Brenner. He was a menacing villain who had purpose and reasons for his experimentations on children and trying to open a gateway to the upside down. Plus we had the Demogorgon, which became a huge costume choice during halloween that year. It's cute that the kids in season 1 called the beast "Demogorgon" and in season 2 started calling the bigger beast "Mind Flayer" because that is their only visual reference they can give it, being fans of Dungeons and Dragons they named those beasts after creatures in D&D.But here in season 3 we have evil Russians being bad for the sake of the 1980's stereotype. This is my one and only problem with this season, a lack of a villain with a purpose. But all that doesn't matter much in the grand scheme of things in the season with the "Mind Flayer" being back. Season 3 definitely improves its writing and storytelling from season 2, even if we put aside evil Russians we still have the introduction of a very well developed Russian scientist. I won't give anymore details about him to keep this spoiler free.Let's go to the mall, and what a mall it is. Starcourt mall is by far one of the best sets, art direction, production design, props, lighting, costumes, extras that I have seen in a series. It is amazing, literally the highlight of the season. They made it feel so authentically 1980's America, licensing dozens of brands to further elevate the authenticity. They didn't just build a set on a sound stage, they found an abandoned mall and built the inside from the ground up, innards, lighting, fixtures, branding, shops etc. They made it a fully functioning mall. That level of detail makes the mall so much more immersive for the viewers and probably for the actors in the scenes as well. For me, the mall was the scene stealer more than anything else. Each character/group goes on their own adventure and purpose to complete a task or uncover some information. There are a few really good plot points and twists and interesting new characters and old recurring characters throughout the season and it felt so wholesome. The second half of the season is much stronger and even got me quite emotional.Rating: I'm giving Stranger Things Season 3 an 8.5 out of 10.
After 3 seasons this show doesn't just feel like a one hit wonder, although with a slightly rocky second season, season 3 comes back to form and delivers a satisfying narrative reminiscent of season 1. Even without a purposeful/menacing human villain this season still goes strong with tons of 80's nostalgia and easter eggs. If you have seen season 1 & 2 you will want to see this season as it is not a disappointment. Lucas's younger sister Erica, is another scene stealer along with the Russian scientist Alexei. Keep an eye out for those characters as you watch the season.

content: Stranger Things is the newest foray into Netflix's original programming, of which brings us their most impressive- and strange- production to date. When a young boy named Will Byers goes missing, his friends, mother and the town are thrust into a conspiracy involving a mysterious girl named Eleven and something even more sinister hiding in the woods of Hawkins, Indiana.From the get-go, you can tell this is an homage to classic '80s Spielberg, drawing on E.T. and Close Encounters, as well as JJ Abrams' Super 8. But, as the show progresses, it becomes more and more like a twisted Stephen King story set in a Spielberg movie. It becomes a dark and twisted ride into an even darker and more disturbing world where the stakes feel higher than anything before it.I can't go into great detail because spoiling even just a bit of the story takes away from the greater mystery, but I can say, it's one of the most thrilling and intense series to be on TV, without being on TV. If it were to continue, they have to pull the same punches they did with the first season, because they took a great many clichés, and somehow made them fresh and surprising, save for just a couple that they purposefully left cliché.

author: johannes2000-1
title: More and more disappointing!
content: With such a high rating as 8.7 (t the moment I write this review) it seems like being a sourpuss or a nitpicker to have even the slightest reservations, but I still feel the need to get them off my chest.Yes, all 4 seasons are very impressive, evolving from funny horror stuff for kids to almost epic proportions in the last season (even the duration of the last episodes being epic!). But as things grew bigger and bigger, I personally more and more lost my touch with the story as well as with all the characters, especially in season 4 where things got totally chaotic. Way too many characters, operating on way too many levels in way too many bizarre storylines, it was all extremely hard to follow, made even more difficult by the constant shifting between the present and the past or by things happening in real life and things happening in a state of... I mostly couldn't event tell: dream? Subconsciousness? Parallel life??Sure, there were some nice, scary scenes and the CGI was at many times great, but Vecna himself, who should be the epitome of Most Fearsome Being Ever, looked most of the time just like someone in a not very scary black suit. Then there was this time-consuming second storyline in Russia, with endless depressing scenes of Jim in prison where hardly anything happened (until at last, but totally out of the blue, the monsters appeared!), and only in the very last episode they came up with a rather contrived link to Vecna.All those kids that were so funny and endearing in the first season, in season 4 seemed to have grown into a bunch of rather poorly acting young adults, who were still made to come up with corny primary-school humor. Supposed heroin Millie Bobby Brown in my opinion can only put up two expressions: either a wide-eyed cry-face or an (intended) intense face, and her parading in several curious, unbecoming outfits, with constantly stretched-out arm to evoke her powers, was more laughable than impressive.If the already announced season 5 will go further down this slope, I'll definitely give it up.

author: robertodovalefilho
title: It starts well, but it only gets worse. Both the script and the characters
content: Stranger Things starts very strong. The first season is engaging, atmospheric, and almost every character feels interesting and well-balanced. However, as the show progresses, each new season introduces more and more characters, to the point where it becomes tiring and unnecessary, hurting the focus of the story.Another major issue is the excessive comic relief. Many moments that should build tension are interrupted by exaggerated jokes, which end up breaking the suspense instead of enhancing it. This tonal imbalance becomes more noticeable over time.Robin is a clear example of this problem. In season 3, she is smart, charismatic, and refreshing. In later seasons, however, her personality is pushed too far, making her extremely annoying and repetitive.By the time season 5 arrives, Stranger Things has largely lost its original spark. What once felt fresh and exciting now feels overextended, relying too much on nostalgia, humor, and an overcrowded cast rather than strong storytelling.

author: Sayan07PM
title: It Started With Friendship, Ended With Acceptance - And Left Us With a Truth We Were Never Ready to Face."
content:
Stranger Things was never truly about monsters, alternate dimensions, or horror.It was about childhood.About a time when life was simple. Riding bicycles, playing games, reading comics, laughing without knowing what fear really meant. It was about a group of kids who lived in a small town where nothing ever seemed wrong, until one day, everything was.Will's disappearance wasn't just the beginning of a story. It was the end of innocence. From that moment, the world changed for them. And slowly, across seasons, it changed for us too. We didn't just watch them grow up. We grew up with them.The finale didn't try to be loud.It didn't try to shock us with twists or satisfy every theory.Instead, it chose something far more powerful. Truth.The Duffer Brothers didn't create a perfect ending.They created a real one.They showed us that life doesn't always give answers.That some wounds never fully heal.That some stories don't end with happiness. They end with acceptance.Henry was never a monster in the traditional sense.He was different. Alone. Misunderstood.And when the Mind Flayer found him, it didn't create evil. It amplified pain.He became a weapon not because he wanted destruction, but because grief consumed him.And once someone is swallowed by grief that deep, even regret becomes powerless.That's the tragedy of Henry.Not a villain who chose darkness, but a soul who couldn't escape it.And the kids, every single one of them, had their moment.Lucas, loving Max with a loyalty that never faded, even when hope was almost gone.Max, trapped and broken, yet still fighting to live.Dustin, the heart of the group, carrying intelligence, humor, and loyalty like armor.Will, finally standing up to his fears, his emotions, his truth.Mike, often misunderstood, yet quietly holding everyone together with love and belief.Steve, the protector no one expected, becoming the brother and hero everyone needed.Nancy, fearless and driven.Jonathan, sacrificing his own happiness for the people he loved.And Eleven.She lost her mother.Her childhood.Her peace.Her normal life.Again and again.Yet she still chose to walk forward.Not as a weapon.Not as a monster.But as a human being learning to live with loss.And that is why this ending hurts in the best way.Because it tells us something most stories avoid saying:
This ending deserves applause for showing the raw truth of life that we don't always get what we want, and we don't always get to spend our lives with the ones most special to us. It's the curse of life we're all aware of, yet still refuse to believe. This reality is what the ending truly portrayed. Wasn't this the whole point?That line alone explains everything.This wasn't a story about saving the world.It was about growing up and realizing you can't save everything.People drift apart.Dreams change.Love remains, even when people don't.And the most beautiful part?It all ended where it began.In the basement.Where friends laughed.Where dice rolled.Where imagination lived.Where childhood was still alive.Just like Lost, this ending wasn't about answers. It was about meaning.But in its own way, Stranger Things went even deeper.It reminded us that life doesn't owe us closure. Only moments.And those moments, the bikes, the laughter, the tears, the sacrifices, they stay with us forever.This wasn't just a series.It was a memory.A goodbye.A reminder.And honestly, no one could have loved this story better than the people who made it.

author: RyanWinter100
title: Best of TV...
content:
Stranger Things is the most refreshing piece of TV work that I have seen in a very long time. I'm a TV-aholic and an avid movie fan. Stranger Things has manage to combine the best of both mediums. First and foremost, The Duffer Brothers have given us a very good story. It's crafted well with a realistic but dark location. The photography is superb, that along with the production design creates a terrific canvas for the odd tale. The casting is absolutely perfect. Each actor, young and old, fits beautifully into their segment of this simple but multi-level story. The special effects are eerie, bold and effective. The music is minimal which plays well into the overall presentation. When I watch TV much of the time, I might be on my computer simultaneoulsy. I have managed over the years to do both pretty well at the same time. But when I'm watching Stranger Things, I turn the computer off. I find the show absolutely compelling and I don't want to miss a single frame. 
This is the first Netflix show I've ever watched. Truthfully, I didn't know what to expect, but I assumed it would be of lower quality than network shows. To my surprise and delight, the production values are far superior to any network program. You can feel the thinking and sincere desire of the creators constantly as you watch.
I have to admit I love the young people in the show. Oh, the adults are excellent, but the four boys and the two girls are engaging and they are valid portrayals of young people. Dustin curses and without making jokes is absolutely hilarious, Luke gets angry but is loyal, Mike wants to lead and he leads well, Will is sweet and so vulnerable, Max (a girl) is all those things, and poor mysterious Eleven is so wounded inwardly that if and when she smiles, just for a second, your heart is warmed.
I have only one complaint about this show--there are so few episodes to view. Networks give you 22-24 shows per season. As of late 2017, after two seasons, there is only 17 of these brilliant productions. Now you don't want to rush the producers into creating more just to have more; you want them to maintain the quality. But guys, can't you at least give us 10 episodes per season?
Stranger things deserves every award out there for outstanding acting, writing, directing, photography and acting.
I hope it stays with us for a long time.

author: Artifam
title: Only Good Things
content: Goonies, IT, E.T., Stand by Me and Dungeons & Dragons... you name it, Stranger Things is an amalgamation of some fantastic legendary '80s adventure and coming of age movies. Spielberg and JJ Abram's Super8 film in 2011 did a similar thing (albeit set in 1979), but Stranger Things is more indulgent story-line given the full series treatment to tell its tale, then expand further in a richer and deeper second series (and now a third newly commissioned). What makes it so special is that it ticks so many boxes. The characters are well developed and very likeable (or suitably loathsome) and sourcing largely unknown actors (excluding Winona Ryder) works incredibly well at avoiding any preconceptions and typecasting. The music is simply fantastic, leading with its bassy electro intro credits it sets an eerily brooding and foreboding tone before hitting you with an 'old school type-font chapter screen that sucks the viewer straight back in time and into the damned village of Hawkins, just like the town of Derry in IT and from there it's a nostalgic mix of crude haircuts, BMX bikes, walkie-talkies, sneaking around parents, and strange goings-on that bond friends closer and strangers ever nearer in a supernatural adventure that presses all the buttons without ever feeling contrived or corny. Intelligent use of music, be it background tracks composed for the show or insertions of '80s classic hits proficiently build the mood, and when it comes specifically to moments of suspense its clever camera-work expertly delivers the thrills and shocks, even if you're expecting the monster or baddie to appear. All in all, it's just a fantastic nostalgic fun adventure.

author: atharvshrivastav
title: Waste of time
content: Stranger Things is often praised as a groundbreaking series, but beneath the hype lies a painfully overrated and repetitive show that survives more on nostalgia than genuine storytelling. The series relies heavily on 1980s references, not as meaningful context, but as a lazy distraction to mask weak writing and predictable plots. Instead of creating original ideas, it endlessly recycles clichés from old sci-fi and horror films, offering little innovation of its own.The storyline becomes increasingly absurd with each season. What begins as a mysterious disappearance quickly turns into a chaotic mess of monsters, secret labs, and supernatural powers that make no logical sense. The rules of the "Upside Down" change whenever convenient, destroying any sense of consistency. Rather than building suspense, the show repeats the same formula every season: a monster appears, characters scream, Eleven saves the day, and everything resets.Character development is another major flaw. Many characters feel one-dimensional and exaggerated, existing only to serve the plot. Emotional moments are forced and overdramatic, making them feel artificial rather than impactful. The constant use of fake-out deaths further ruins tension, as the audience quickly realizes that no major character is ever truly at risk.The pacing is painfully uneven. Episodes drag on with unnecessary subplots and filler scenes that add nothing to the main story. Action sequences are loud but empty, relying on flashy visuals instead of meaningful stakes. Even the dialogue often feels childish and repetitive, failing to match the dark tone the show tries so hard to create.Ultimately, Stranger Things is a show that mistakes style for substance. It may look impressive on the surface, but once the nostalgia wears off, what remains is a shallow, predictable, and increasingly exhausting series that simply refuses to know when to end.

author: hyzgqns
title: The best show of my life
content: Why Stranger Things Is the Best Show of My LifeStranger Things is more than a television series; it is a complete emotional and narrative experience that combines storytelling, atmosphere, character development, and cultural impact in a way very few shows ever achieve. From its first episode, the series establishes a unique identity that remains consistent while continuously evolving across seasons.One of the strongest reasons Stranger Things stands out is its exceptional storytelling. The show masterfully blends science fiction, horror, mystery, and coming-of-age drama into a cohesive narrative. Each season builds upon the previous one, expanding the mythology of the Upside Down while maintaining clear emotional stakes. The plot is suspenseful without being confusing, and every mystery feels earned rather than forced.Another defining strength is its characters. The group of kids-Mike, Eleven, Dustin, Lucas, and Will-feel authentic, relatable, and deeply human. Their friendships are the emotional core of the series. As the characters grow older, the show allows them to mature naturally, dealing with loss, trauma, love, and identity. Eleven's journey, in particular, is one of the most powerful character arcs in modern television, exploring themes of belonging, abuse, and self-acceptance.The emotional impact of Stranger Things is unmatched. The series is not afraid to be dark, tragic, or painful, but it balances those moments with humor, warmth, and hope. Deaths and sacrifices matter, and consequences are permanent. This emotional honesty creates a strong connection between the viewer and the story, making moments of triumph feel genuinely rewarding.The atmosphere and aesthetics also play a major role in making the show unforgettable. The 1980s setting is not just nostalgic decoration; it is integrated into the storytelling through music, costumes, cinematography, and cultural references. The soundtrack, in particular, elevates the tension and emotion of key scenes, turning many moments into iconic television history.From a technical perspective, Stranger Things delivers cinematic-level production quality. The visual effects, sound design, and set pieces rival major Hollywood films. Each season feels larger and more ambitious, yet the show never loses focus on its characters or emotional core.Finally, Stranger Things succeeds because of its heart. At its core, the show is about friendship, loyalty, love, and standing up to overwhelming darkness together. It reminds viewers that even in the face of fear and loss, human connection is the most powerful force of all.For these reasons-its storytelling, characters, emotional depth, atmosphere, and timeless themes-Stranger Things is not just a great series. It is the best show of my life.

author: AlishaZ-1
title: Lagendry series
content: Stranger Things: A Whisper from the Upside DownIn the sleepy town of Hawkins, where bikes rule and walkie-talkies whisper secrets, the ordinary cracks-and something extraordinary seeps through. Stranger Things is not just a TV series; it's a vortex of nostalgia, monsters, and heart.Imagine if Spielberg and Stephen King had a dream. That dream would be this show.At first glance, it's about missing kids, awkward teens, and telekinesis. But beneath the flickering lights and synth-heavy soundtrack lies a masterclass in storytelling. The Duffer Brothers craft a world where every character breathes-with all their flaws, fears, and fierce love. Eleven, the girl with a bleeding nose and a haunted past, becomes both weapon and wonder. Joyce, a mother on the edge, turns madness into maternal magic.And then there's the Mind Flayer, the Demogorgon-the monsters we see. But the true terror? It's the darkness inside people, the kind that turns science into cruelty, friendship into fear.Yet, light always fights back. Through every upside-down moment, it's the bonds-between friends, families, and misfits-that light the way. There's pain, yes, but also pancakes, D&D, and never letting go.Stranger Things isn't just binge-worthy. It's a mirror held to childhood, to courage, to the monsters within and the magic around.So switch off the lights. Plug in the fairy lamps. And listen-can you hear it? The Upside Down is calling.

author: evgeny_k
title: Great series, great acting !
content: Stranger things is a product of 2016 and people should pay attention to this. It surely used old well-known elements or settings from the 1980s but I believe that people should stop thinking of films in the 80s and stop comparing it to them. Let us take a look at the series objectively and from the modern point of view ! Surely it belongs to a genre that was started a long time ago and the 1980 nostalgia exists but please do not overreact because of this fact. Analyzing STRANGER THINGS in short: 1. The most important part of a cinema masterpiece or a TV series is the script. The script is just great, keeps you interested and does not involve retarded mistakes or plot holes. Some scenes might develop in a more obvious way that I like (i.e. not so original) and some words might not be the perfect choice in some cases /IMHO at least/... Then again originality is rarer than gold these days. But to be honest the script as a whole is just fine through the whole season 1. The script here lays a great and sturdy foundation of the "family house" the creators are building. A house of mystery, fear and bravery, of action and of basic human emotions. 2. The actors are amazing. The kids are natural, Dustin in particular is just the kind of kid that people will love and the kind of actor that is acting using his talent and to the best of his ability. Winona Ryder gives us a lot of strong emotions to chew and surely lives up to the image of a movie star she had in the past /and probably never lost/. 3. The effects are probably not the maximum possible movie high-tech wonder but they look cool and fitting to the main atmosphere. I surely do not expect more of the FX team for season 2. 4. The more you watch, the more interested you are. It does not get boring. Stranger Things does not crumble because of some soap opera motives like ARROW did. 5. You just have to like kids and sci-fi to watch, if you do not like kids just get out of here. :) ------------------------------------- Obvviously it is not plausible to just talk about what I liked about Stranger Things so let me point out some weak spots: - the bad guys often behave in a stupid and inert way - the cop sometimes takes weird decisions - several things in the last episode were very unacceptable, I don't wish to include spoilers...If Game of Thrones should get the gold medal for the best series of 2016, Stranger Things goes home with the silver ! 9/10

author: hanschsolo
title: An dragged Spectacle
content: Stranger Things stumbles upon it's own feet.It got great Character-Work, great Atmosphere and was made with so much care in the first season. It feels believable and alive. And even the further 4 seasons proved this, the sudden tone changes are distracting and out of place sometimes, but it's the vibe, and I get that they want to deliver a different feeling in each season.But that's not the same with season 5. Character Arcs don't develop or go further, dynamics don't expand, views and morals are not challenged or changed, stranger things has lost everything that made it special. It was human and even in its weirdness, it was still believable. Season 5 just feels like an long expansion of season 4, it's always the same structure.They have a plan, they explain it, they have a few problems to solve, and then when they execute the plan the things are different than thought (packed as a slight plot twist) and the circumstances change. Tell me I'm wrong, but this is basically episode 1 to 7 in this final season. It's world just feels empty, not believable anymore.It doesn't feel like great storytelling anymore, and I can tell for sure it isn't. Characters are protected by insane plot armor, actions are not logical anymore, character interactions feel unnatural and forced, and there's a lot of plot holes in character dynamics and world-building, a lot of inconsistency. Why?Because of spectacle. But spectacle isn't what this show is about, it's about character. We love stranger things not for the Demogorgons or Vecna, we don't love it because of the mystery aspect or plot, who cares about the Russian sub plot or the whole military sub plot? It's about character dynamics, we grew up basically WITH these characters, and we wanna see how these dynamics turn out under these critical circumstances. It's not that anymore, it's a franchise, an IP. Character's can't be challenged or killed, they get revived or protected insanely much.I haven't seen the final episode but It basically can't change much, my only hope is that they wrap up the plot logically, but we for sure can see that this wasn't planned out from the beginning, and they make it like It was. It feels horribly pretentious. I love the series for what it was, but what it became shows, that we need to change cinema and shows for the better. More into character, less into spectacle.

author: MarkT-687
title: It's good.
content: The Duffer Brothers deliver a fitting capstone in Season 5, scaling up the stakes while returning to the intimate character dynamics that defined the early years. "Sorcerer" remains a standout for its logistical ambition-an Upside Down assault rivaling any prior set piece-yet the true power lies in the finale, "The Rightside Up."Millie Bobby Brown's Eleven reaches full apotheosis in her confrontation with Vecna, a sequence that balances raw psychic spectacle with genuine pathos. The ensemble work shines: Harbour and Ryder anchor the adult line with weathered gravitas, while the original kids-Wolfhard, Schnapp, McLaughlin, Matarazzo, Sink-deliver performances matured beyond their years, particularly Schnapp's understated Will arc. Nostalgia is deployed judiciously rather than indiscriminately; the synth score and '80s references enhance rather than overwhelm. Plot threads converge satisfyingly, resolving the Mind Flayer/Vecna hierarchy without cheap cop-outs, and the epilogue provides closure while leaving just enough ambiguity. Flaws are minor-occasional pacing lulls in the mid-season-but they pale against the overall achievement. Stranger Things exits at its peak: ambitious, heartfelt, and unapologetically entertaining. Essential viewing.

author: edvardogomes
title: A Thrilling, Nostalgic Ride That Occasionally Trips on Its Own Growth.
content: Stranger Things is a love letter to '80s pop culture wrapped in supernatural mystery, endearing characters, and pure adrenaline. It starts as a small-town story about a missing boy and spirals into an epic tale of alternate dimensions, shady government labs, and coming-of-age struggles - all held together by a core cast that's nothing short of iconic.The first and fourth seasons shine brightest, blending tension, emotional depth, and stylish horror with skill. Season 1 is tight and haunting, while Season 4 raises the stakes and the scares, thanks to a terrifying new villain and standout performances (especially from Sadie Sink and Joseph Quinn). Season 2, though a bit repetitive at times, still delivers great moments and strong character development.Season 3, however, is where the show stumbles. While it's visually polished and full of fun, the tonal shift leans too heavily into comedy and neon gloss, occasionally undercutting the stakes and emotional weight. The Russian subplot and mall setting, while entertaining, feel like a step away from the eerie intimacy that made the earlier seasons so gripping.Still, the emotional core - the friendships, the found family, the fight against darkness - remains strong.8.5/10 - a thrilling, stylish, and heart-filled series that captures both the nostalgia and the nightmares of youth, even if it briefly loses its footing in the middle.Whether in Hawkins or the Upside Down, Stranger Things knows how to keep us watching.

author: mskate82
title: Well-acted and nostalgic, Stranger Things is (mostly) a winner
content: First and foremost, Stranger Things is a very entertaining show. The acting, 80's references and a general lighthearted tone all mash to make a compelling show. The entire first season is about find Will Byers, a 12 year old boy that disappeared into the "Upside Down" a alternate dimension that corresponds with our world. After Will disappears, his friends find a girl (nicknamed Eleven) that says she knows where Will is. There are subplots that interlock with the story that are all interesting.When I first heard about the show, the idea of a show built around child actor worried me a bit. Child actors, mostly, fall into two categories: genuine and disingenuous. Luckily the excellent direction from the Duffer Brothers and the performances from the kids fall into the former. 80's culture is perfectly ingrained into the story. There isn't too many, nor are they made the focal point of show. The film grain on the show is subtle enough to be noticeable to the audience, but again, is not too obvious. The music is mostly good, but it can be too electronic at times.My problems with the show start with the demogorgon, a monster that lives in the Upside Down. **Minor spoilers** The demogorgon comes into real life through the wall in a sequence that feels like a bad sequel to The Last of Us. The build up for the creature is immense, but both the look and actions of the monster fall flat. Scenes like this lack real stakes, and this does not have much tension. **Major Spoilers** The last major scene has Eleven sacrifice herself to the demogorgon as she disappeared into the Upside Down. This was entirely forced and contrived. The series builds Eleven as essential to the puzzle that is the Upside Down, but this scene uses her as a plot device. It is your classic set up for another season that shies away from themes introduced through the entire season. It's a shame.But those are just a few of my complaints. I doubt most people will have a problem with them. Overall though, it's just such a fun show to watch and I'm excited to see where it goes. Happy Bingeing!

author: imdbfan-2330470869
title: The series is legendary
content: A Personal Take on "Stranger Things" - A Masterpiece of Nostalgia and Mystery**I consider *Stranger Things* a masterpiece that brilliantly blends science fiction, horror, and drama. From the moment I started watching, I couldn't stop thinking about its gripping plot and unforgettable characters. The show transports viewers back to the 1980s, capturing every nostalgic detail-from its synth-heavy soundtrack to clever nods to classics like *E. T.* and *The Goonies*. The story revolves around the disappearance of a boy named Will Byers and the bizarre supernatural events that unfold in the small town of Hawkins.What truly sets this series apart, in my opinion, are its characters. The core group of kids-Mike, Dustin, Lucas, and Eleven-are written with such authenticity that you feel like you've known them forever. Eleven, portrayed by Millie Bobby Brown, is especially mesmerizing, thanks to her mysterious past and extraordinary abilities. The adult characters, like Joyce Byers (Winona Ryder) and Chief Hopper (David Harbour), add emotional depth with their raw performances. Joyce's desperate search for her son and Hopper's gruff-but-caring demeanor make the story resonate on a deeply human level.Beyond the thrills, *Stranger Things* explores themes of friendship, family, and resilience in the face of adversity. The eerie atmosphere, paired with stunning visuals and seamless special effects, makes every episode immersive. Each season builds on the last, unraveling new secrets and expanding the show's lore, which keeps me eagerly awaiting the next chapter.

author: DarklyDreamingFan
title: A thrilling, emotional, era-defining adventure that will be remembered for decades
content:
A genre-defining cultural phenomenon packed with heart, mystery, spectacle, and one of TV's most beloved ensembles. A near-perfect fusion of horror, adventure, and '80s sentimentality..🎬 Series Summary (Spoiler-Free)
Stranger Things begins with the disappearance of Will Byers, a quiet kid in the sleepy town of Hawkins, Indiana. What seems like a typical missing-person case soon unravels into a nightmare of:Secret government experiments; A psychic girl known only as Eleven; A monstrous alternate dimension called The Upside Down And a chain of supernatural threats that grow more terrifying with each season.As Hawkins' kids, Mike, Lucas, Dustin, Will, and Eleven, fight back, they forge a found family built on loyalty and courage. Meanwhile:Joyce becomes the town's relentless protector.Hopper battles both demons and fatherhood.Nancy, Steve, Jonathan, and Robin evolve into monster-hunting veterans.New allies like Max and Eddie reshape the emotional core.The stakes escalate from one missing boy to global catastrophe as creatures, curses, and interdimensional horrors push Hawkins toward apocalyptic collapse.It's a story of growing up in the shadow of darkness and choosing to stand together anyway..✅ What Worked1. One of the strongest ensemble casts in modern TV2. Eleven's powerful, emotional hero arc3. Sharp blend of horror, adventure, and heart4. Immaculate '80s nostalgia: music, fashion, cinematography5. Brilliant creature design and VFX6. Deep emotional bonds: friendship, family, found-family7. Unforgettable moments (Demogorgon fight, Mind Flayer battles, Vecna's curse)8. Iconic soundtrack and needle drops ("Running Up That Hill," "Master of Puppets").❌ What Didn't Work1. Some mid-series pacing slowdowns2. A few character arcs get sidelined in later seasons3. Repetitive "kids split up, reunite, save the world" structure4. Large cast occasionally strains screen time balance5. Season 4's episodes, while excellent, are extremely long.💬 Favorite Moments (Spoiler-Free)1. Eleven discovering her powers2. The kids' D&D parallels to real threats3. Steve's unlikely evolution into a fan-favorite hero4. Joyce's Christmas light communication with Will5. Max's "Running Up That Hill" sequence6. Eddie's rooftop guitar moment: iconic7. Hopper and Eleven's heartfelt father-daughter scenes8. Major season finales filled with emotional punches and epic action.✨ Fun Facts1. Millie Bobby Brown shaved her head at age 11 for the role.2. The Duffers pitched the series as "Stephen King meets Steven Spielberg."3. Kate Bush's "Running Up That Hill" surged to #1 globally after Season 4.4. Eddie Munson was inspired by real '80s metal culture and the "Satanic Panic."5. Hopper's cabin was built in the middle of a Georgia forest and can be visited.6. The show's Demogorgon originally used practical effects before heavy CGI.7. Many Hawkins locations are real buildings in Atlanta that fans now pilgrimage to..👀 If You Liked This, You Might Also Enjoy1. The X-Files2. It (2017 + 2019)3. Super 84. Dark5. Buffy the Vampire Slayer6. Locke & Key7. The OA.🎯 Final Thoughts
Stranger Things is a rare cultural lightning bolt. A show that combines blockbuster thrills with unforgettable emotional depth. It's nostalgic yet innovative, frightening yet heartwarming, and driven by one of the best casts of young actors ever assembled. Few series manage to feel so epic and so intimate at the same time.⭐ 9.4/10. A thrilling, emotional, era-defining adventure that will be remembered for decades.

author: Balzs-9
title: Old fan
content:
Guys, I just finished Stranger Things.It was so incredibly good that I'm crying, but I'm also happy-so honestly, I don't even know how to feel.It's such a strange feeling to see something end that I started watching 10 years ago, and today the series has officially come to an end.It's crazy how much time has passed from the first season to the fifth. So much happened-so many different storylines, so many emotions: excitement, laughter, tears. And it's so surreal to see how the kids I once watched on screen grew up... and how we grew up with them too (those of us who've been watching since the beginning).So yes, it's both amazing and heartbreaking that something has truly and finally come to an end.It's wild-and also kind of beautiful.I'm so grateful that I could experience this series so deeply. The creators came up with an insanely good story and found actors who performed their roles so professionally that they genuinely pulled out exactly the emotions they wanted from the audience. Hats off to them for directing such a powerful series so brilliantly. It became something truly special and fills me with happiness. I can honestly recommend it to anyone who hasn't seen it yet.Of course, not everyone can fully immerse themselves in a series-but for those who can feel stories deeply and connect with emotions, I highly recommend it. And the fact that this was a show that lasted 10 years and accompanied me through my own life makes it even more meaningful to me. That's why it hits so hard. For me, it's just... the ultimate.And yes, I absolutely love every single actor-everyone delivered an outstanding performance! Hats off to all of them!Jamie Campbell Bower as Vecna was an incredible choice for the main villain.And Joyce Byers-Winona Ryder-is simply a perfect actress. The amount I cried because of her, and the strength she gave me, that unstoppable mother energy-"I'll do it no matter what"-was just amazing.I'm deeply grateful to the Duffer Brothers for creating this incredible series, and to all the actors who were unbelievably talented. Outstanding. Perfect.Watch it too if my opinion made you curiousThank you. Thank you. And thank you.A fan from Hungary 🇭🇺
-Balazs.

author: berfin_erdem
title: Loved it !!!
content: Love the cast, the set, the storyline, the music (try playing the theme song in Spotify and watch what happens)At first, I doubted that I would find this show interesting, because it follows kids/preteens. However, with such a talented cast (and they're only kids!!) I was hooked. Especially Noah Schnapp, he amazes me every time. It has everything. It's beautifully made, it's scary but also emotional, it's full of horror but also speaks to your heart. If you haven't already, go watch it, you won't regret. The Duffer Brothers has done an amazing job.However, there are one thing that saddens me, which doesn't have anything to do with the show itself. The very popular Millie Bobby Brown is getting paid a lot more (300.000 $ per episode) than her costars, Gaten Matarazzo, Finn Wolfhard, Caleb McLaughlin and Noah Schnapps (200.000-250.000 $ per episode) in season 2 and perhaps afterwards. I think that's unfair, because yes she is talented, but so are the other kids. She is on the screen just as much as her other costars. I know her character is different, expressing emotions through her facial expression and therefore harder to do, but with her having like no lines, it outweighs and therefore has the same amount of work as the other kids.A lot of people keep saying that Stranger Things is nothing without Millie and they wouldn't be watching it if she wasn't in it, but I disagree. I wouldn't want to watch the series, if it only focused on her character. I think the ensemble cast is what makes this series so good, and therefore the whole cast deserves just as much praise as her. Literally all the attention is on her these days. Don't get me wrong, she is an amazing actress and does a lot for the show - but not EVERYthing

author: OnlyInThe80s
title: Absolutely Superb from start to finish!
content: As a product of the 80's, I loved every moment of this show.We live in an age where it's easy to write a negative review or label something as a waste of time. But when you place this show against hundreds of others that have been aired over the past decade. You would be hard pushed to find a show that has a better cast, production value, sense of nostalgia, the soundtrack and overall story than stranger things.Stranger things hits every single point. author: tyelder
title: More Than Just 80s Nostalgia: A Bitchin' Show That Changed TV Forever
content: For almost a decade, one story about a group of rag-tag friends from Hawkins, Indiana, redefined what it means to be a pop-culture phenomenon. Stranger Things isn't just a television series; it's a masterclass in storytelling and filmmaking-a monumental masterpiece that juxtaposes themes of loss, trauma, and redemption into a giant, synth-heavy homage to the 1980s.Personally, I began this journey in 2016 at the start of my high school career, only a couple of years older than Mike, Will, Lucas, and Dustin. I could instantly relate to those kids riding across town on their bikes to save their friends. To put the show's personal influence into perspective, I eventually chose to attend the Duffer Brothers' own alma mater, Chapman University, for my Bachelor's degree. Getting to experience the later seasons while at the "hometown" of the creators gave me a unique appreciation for the superior quality and craftsmanship Matt and Ross Duffer brought to every frame.From the iconic 'Stephen King font' title crawl to the eerie, enigmatic score by Kyle Dixon and Michael Stein, the show sets a mood that is impossible to look away from. The Duffers, alongside Shawn Levy, utilized Spielberg-inspired transitions and a "creature feature" horror aesthetic that broke down the barriers of what a "streaming show" could be. It never felt like a disposable series; it felt like a decades-long movie that blossomed into a grandiose tale of the Upside Down.Characters are the heart of Hawkins. The casting was astounding-from the breakout performances of Millie Bobby Brown and Finn Wolfhard to the career-defining work of Winona Ryder and David Harbour. What makes the show special is how it treated its supporting cast. Characters like Steve Harrington and Nancy Wheeler weren't pushed aside; they were given individual story arcs that earned their ultimate fates. Whether it was the addition of 80s icons like Sean Astin and Matthew Modine or new favorites like Sadie Sink and Maya Hawke, the world always felt lived-in and authentic.The soundtrack-which I've proudly collected on vinyl-is integral to the experience. Whether it was the emotional weight of Peter Gabriel's "Heroes" or the tearful goodbyes set to Prince's "Purple Rain," the music elevated the stakes. This all culminated in an unprecedented final season released in three massive volumes. Getting to witness the finale in a movie theater with over 3,500 people was a shared emotional climax unlike anything else in TV history. It was a movie in every sense of the word.Stranger Things changed the way we consume and create television. It turned Netflix into a powerhouse studio and proved that an epic story about characters we care about will always be the most important part of entertainment. Saying goodbye to this world is hard, but just like the Hellfire Club, I choose to continue to believe.

author: imdbfan-93555
title: Stranger Things
content: Stranger Things is a nostalgic, thrilling series that masterfully blends science fiction, horror, and coming-of-age drama. Its greatest strengths lie in its engaging cast, atmospheric 1980s setting, and emotionally driven storytelling. The show's ability to build suspense and develop deep bonds between characters-especially the core group of kids-has been a major factor in its popularity. The visual effects and soundtrack further enhance its distinct tone and style.However, as the seasons progress, the show occasionally struggles with pacing and balancing its expanding ensemble cast. Some subplots can feel repetitive or underdeveloped, and at times the emotional impact is diluted by an overreliance on action or spectacle. Additionally, while the nostalgia is part of its charm, it sometimes leans too heavily on references instead of pushing the story forward.Overall, Stranger Things remains an entertaining and emotionally resonant series that captures both adventure and heart. With tighter storytelling and more balanced character focus, it can continue to grow while maintaining its original magic.

author: kumadan
title: Season 3 Review (Spoiler Free)
content:
Disclaimer: As stated in the title this is a spoiler free review of Stranger Things Season 3 but I will be talking about plot points and minor spoilers from Season 1 & 2.So Stranger Things 3 picks up where we left off after season 2, everyone is happy and everyone is together, there is love in the air, it is the summer of love. Right off the bat I can say I preferred this season over season 2. This season felt more contained, it felt like it had a purpose and knew what it was doing and where is was going. Season 2 for me felt more of a mess, especially with "The Lost Sister" filler episode. The reviews of that episode tanked so hard that the writers completely gave up on that subplot, and I'm glad they did. That is one of the many reasons season 3 feels so much more crisp, because Matt and Ross Duffer decided to be more focused on the main story.As always the cast this season is great, the kids are now older and feel more like seasoned actors and much more mature in their performances. The kids stand out and shine more in this season especially with the addition of a couple of new characters. The adult characters are great as well, but a lot of them (apart from the main ones) felt wasted and underdeveloped. For example, in true 1980's form, we have evil Russians, which sounds hilarious but falls flat. The reason season 1 shined more than this or season 2 is because it had a well defined shadowy government department with a leader who was well developed. Remember "papa" from season 1? aka Dr. Martin Brenner. He was a menacing villain who had purpose and reasons for his experimentations on children and trying to open a gateway to the upside down. Plus we had the Demogorgon, which became a huge costume choice during halloween that year. It's cute that the kids in season 1 called the beast "Demogorgon" and in season 2 started calling the bigger beast "Mind Flayer" because that is their only visual reference they can give it, being fans of Dungeons and Dragons they named those beasts after creatures in D&D.But here in season 3 we have evil Russians being bad for the sake of the 1980's stereotype. This is my one and only problem with this season, a lack of a villain with a purpose. But all that doesn't matter much in the grand scheme of things in the season with the "Mind Flayer" being back. Season 3 definitely improves its writing and storytelling from season 2, even if we put aside evil Russians we still have the introduction of a very well developed Russian scientist. I won't give anymore details about him to keep this spoiler free.Let's go to the mall, and what a mall it is. Starcourt mall is by far one of the best sets, art direction, production design, props, lighting, costumes, extras that I have seen in a series. It is amazing, literally the highlight of the season. They made it feel so authentically 1980's America, licensing dozens of brands to further elevate the authenticity. They didn't just build a set on a sound stage, they found an abandoned mall and built the inside from the ground up, innards, lighting, fixtures, branding, shops etc. They made it a fully functioning mall. That level of detail makes the mall so much more immersive for the viewers and probably for the actors in the scenes as well. For me, the mall was the scene stealer more than anything else. Each character/group goes on their own adventure and purpose to complete a task or uncover some information. There are a few really good plot points and twists and interesting new characters and old recurring characters throughout the season and it felt so wholesome. The second half of the season is much stronger and even got me quite emotional.Rating: I'm giving Stranger Things Season 3 an 8.5 out of 10.
After 3 seasons this show doesn't just feel like a one hit wonder, although with a slightly rocky second season, season 3 comes back to form and delivers a satisfying narrative reminiscent of season 1. Even without a purposeful/menacing human villain this season still goes strong with tons of 80's nostalgia and easter eggs. If you have seen season 1 & 2 you will want to see this season as it is not a disappointment. Lucas's younger sister Erica, is another scene stealer along with the Russian scientist Alexei. Keep an eye out for those characters as you watch the season.

author: MAK_FlicksIMDb
title: "Six Years With Stranger Things A Series That Became a Part of My Life"
content: Stranger Things is not just a series I watched it's a journey I lived with for almost six years. I followed it patiently, waited through long gaps between seasons, and sometimes even forgot small details because so much time passed. Still, the connection never broke. Maintaining that emotional consistency despite years of waiting is not easy, but this series achieved it beautifully.I started this series long ago, tracked it carefully, even revisited episodes because the memories kept coming back. It reminded me of someone very close to my heartsomeone who understood the series deeply, watched it seriously, and always spoke about it with maturity. Watching it again brought those memories back strongly, making the experience even more personal.What I truly admire is how the series keeps you attached. Yes, at times it slows down and may feel a little boring, but it never lets you leave. Every episode brings a new twist, a new thrill, a new emotional turn. It doesn't waste your time it keeps you seated, invested, and curious.The ending was handled smartly. Some characters were left unexplained, some futures were not shown, and certain storylines were intentionally left open. It feels like the makers left space for the future maybe a new generation, maybe new children, maybe a fresh storyline built on the same universe. Because of this, the story still feels alive.Every character played their role perfectly till the end.Alhamdulillah, it was a satisfying and memorable experience.Stranger Things proves that a series doesn't need constant action to stay powerful it needs heart, consistency, and the ability to stay close to you over time.This is not just entertainment; it's memory, attachment, and emotion.

title: Unity is strength!
content: In small towns, it is often unexpected and unsettling when someone goes missing or when a death occurs, as such events are rare and unusual. When Will disappeared, the sheriff initially assumed that he had either run away or gone to live with his father, dismissing any alternative explanations. However, as strange and unexplainable events began to take place, it became clear that there was more to the situation. The rescue mission to find Will was compelling, particularly because of his mother, Joyce. Despite widespread doubt from those around her, Joyce trusted her maternal intuition, firmly believing that her son was alive and that she was truly communicating with him. Her determination and persistence were central to the search, and with the support of Eleven and Will's friends, she fought tirelessly to bring him back. As the series progresses, the threats from the monsters intensify, often manifesting through the use of a human vessel. Each season showcases the growing strength of these creatures, yet what remains most striking is the way the group consistently unites to confront and overcome them. This collective effort highlights the resilience of the characters and reinforces one of the show's most powerful themes: the strength found in loyalty, friendship, and perseverance.
